D: A South Boston janitor at MIT with a gift for maths has to work out what he actually wants from his life.
P: Pour the black and tans when Will meets Skylar at the Harvard bar.
S: Thin roast beef, barbecue sauce, mayo and cheese on soft rolls, the Kelly's three-way order.

Warm the beef stock in a wide pan, add the sliced beef and heat through for 2 minutes without boiling. Split and lightly toast the rolls, then lay a slice of cheese on each base so it softens. Pile on the beef, then spoon over the barbecue sauce and a little mayo, Kelly's three-way style. Put the lids on and serve hot.
Creamy clam chowder with bacon and potato in cups, Southie in a cup.

Fry the bacon until crisp, then add the onion and celery and cook until soft. Stir in the flour for a minute, then whisk in the clam juice, milk and cream. Add the potatoes and thyme and simmer until the potatoes are tender. Stir in the clams, warm through and season with pepper. Ladle into cups and serve with the crackers.
2 x 290g tins baby clams, juice kept@Seafood
M: Franks with slow golden onions and mustard. Sean gave up his Game 6 seat for a girl.

Cook the onions slowly in the butter with a pinch of salt until soft and golden. Grill or pan-fry the franks, turning, until blistered and hot through. Butter the flat sides of the buns and toast them in the pan until golden. Tuck the franks in and top with onions, mustard and relish.
Corned beef with cabbage, carrots and mustard sauce, Sunday dinner in Southie.

Rinse the silverside, cover with cold water and add the onion, bay leaves, sugar and vinegar. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, barely bubbling, until a skewer slides in easily. Lift the beef out to rest and cook the potatoes and carrots in the liquid. Add the cabbage wedges for the last minutes, then drain and toss with the butter. Warm the cream with the mustard, slice the beef thickly and serve with the vegetables and mustard cream.
W: Caramel apple crumble with vanilla custard
Sticky caramel apples under a buttery crumble, warm vanilla custard. How do you like them apples?

Melt the brown sugar and 60g butter until bubbling, stir in the cream and salt, then toss the apples through. Rub the cold butter into the flour, oats, caster sugar and cinnamon until it clumps. Tip the apples into a baking dish, scatter over the crumble and bake at 180C until golden and bubbling. Warm the custard and serve it over the crumble.
5 Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced@Produce
60g butter, plus 100g cold butter for the crumble@Dairy
K: Pale ale layered under stout in a pint glass, for the night Skylar meets the boys.
Half fill 4 chilled pint glasses with pale ale, tilting the glass as you pour. Pour the stout slowly over the back of a spoon so it sits on top of the ale.
